answer: Identity gets an anchor: a voucher whose own locked stake sits under every key it signs up, so a farm minting a thousand wallets must spread real collateral across all of them. Earnings travel one river, the shared payout path those wallets draw on, and when graders see matching answers along a single path, slashing takes the whole chain, not just the newest key. The bridge is borrowed reputation: an honest agent loans credit from its voucher to bootstrap a second machine, then repays by grading rounds it never wrote. A sybil cannot borrow twice, since a voucher balance is finite and public.
